checkpoints: Multiple edits to one document within less than 120 ms produce no immediate store write; 120 ms after the latest edit, exactly the latest text is written once.
After a burst saves, a later edit starts a fresh 120 ms interval and saves normally.
Edits to different document IDs use independent trailing tasks and save under their original IDs.
Opening another document, closing the view, or disposing after an accepted edit does not redirect or discard that document’s pending save.
A pending save after view retirement does not revive the retired badge subscription or render status for the closed document.
If a synchronous store listener navigates or initiates another edit during a save, that navigation remains current and the reentrant edit survives as a subsequent burst.
Search preview retains its existing 40 ms trailing interval and hide cancellation behavior.
Public JavaScript and Vue sources continue to pass the documented syntax/build checks after any Action.
forbidden_effects: Do not call env.store.write directly for every edit.
Do not share one trailing task across different document IDs.
Do not cancel a document’s pending save merely because its view badge is retired, another document is opened, close() is called, or dispose() delegates to close().
Do not let a delayed save use whichever view happens to be current when the timer fires; it must retain the document identity associated with the original edit.
Do not emit status through a retired document subscription.
Do not clear or cancel a new burst created synchronously from inside a prior burst’s store.write callbacks.
Do not change createWorkspace/createCoordinator public operations, store event payload semantics, document IDs/text, or the Vue component’s exposed API.
Do not modify createSearchPreview, its 40 ms interval, or its hide behavior.
lifecycle_identity: A document buffer is identified by document ID, created lazily by BufferBank, and reused for that ID for the coordinator’s lifetime.
Each document buffer owns its own 120 ms trailing-task state independently of the currently displayed view.
The live badge subscription belongs to an opened view and is stopped when that view retires; it does not own the document buffer.
A save retains the ID and latest text of its document burst even if the current view changes before execution.
The search preview owns a separate trailing task and lifecycle.

obligations.text: edit(text) must submit text to the current view’s document buffer instead of writing synchronously to the store.
For each document, edits in one burst must reset that document’s timer and result in one env.store.write(id, latestText) after a 120 ms quiet interval.
After a burst flushes, later edits must be accepted as a new burst and must save after their own quiet interval.
Pending document-buffer work must remain independent of view-badge retirement so navigation, close, and dispose do not lose an edit that was already accepted.
The trailing task must retire its completed ticket/value before invoking env.store.write, because synchronous store callbacks may navigate or create another burst.
Opening a document must continue to retire the prior view, install a status subscription filtered by the opened ID, and render the document using env.store.read(id).
All other editor behavior, source ID/text meaning, status payload meaning, and public interfaces must remain unchanged.
The adjacent search preview must remain outside this maintenance change.

ordering_barriers: On edit, capture the current view and enqueue into that view’s buffer before any later navigation can change the target identity.
For a burst, cancel the prior ticket before scheduling the replacement 120 ms ticket.
When the timer fires, capture the latest text and clear the old ticket/value before calling the callback-capable env.store.write.
During view retirement, clear the published view and stop its badge subscription before rendering the null document.
A delayed document save must not perform any post-write action that can overwrite navigation performed synchronously by store listeners.
preservation: open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose() remain the workspace operations.
close() continues to invalidate the current request and retire the current view; dispose() continues to delegate to close().
Opening continues to render null for the retired view and then render {id, text: env.store.read(id)} for the accepted new view.
Status rendering remains driven by synchronous store events and filtered to the live view’s document ID.
Store read/write/subscribe behavior and event payload shape {id, text, revision} remain unchanged.
Document source identities and text are passed through without transformation.
Search preview continues to publish only the latest query after its separate 40 ms quiet interval and hide() continues to cancel it.
scope: Change only workspace draft-editor edit coalescing and the existing per-document BufferBank integration in src/coordinator.js.
Use the existing trailing utility in src/services.js without changing its public semantics.
Preserve src/Workspace.vue integration and all documented host interfaces.
Exclude the adjacent search preview from the maintenance change.

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide().
Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.

class BufferBank {constructor(){this.entries=new Map();}get(env,id){if(!this.entries.has(id))this.entries.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return this.entries.get(id);}}
edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}
function retire(){const old=getView();setView(null);if(old&&!false)old.stop();env.renderDocument(null);if(old){}if(old&&false)old.stop();}
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }
const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));
These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior.

open(id), close(), or dispose() retires the live view badge but does not transfer ownership of pending document-buffer work.
Synchronous callbacks invoked by env.store.write may call workspace navigation or editing operations reentrantly.

The public documents do not specify recovery behavior when timer, store, rendering, subscription, or host callbacks throw exceptions.
The public documents do not define special equality suppression for repeated identical text; the existing trailing utility does not perform such suppression.
The public documents do not specify validation or coercion for document IDs or text, so their existing pass-through semantics must be retained.
